papers.abstract: Aberrant splicing, a hallmark of cancer, emerges as a promising therapeutic target and is driven by dysregulated expression and mutations in splicing machinery components. Despite exhibiting minimal mutations in splicing factors, T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) critically relies on splicing perturbations. However, the mechanistic underpinnings remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that T cell malignancies display the most prevalent splicing alterations and heterogeneity across cancer types, leading to a substantial overproduction of splice variants. SAP30BP, frequently overexpressed in T-ALL, actively contributes to this process and aggravates T cell tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, SAP30BP coordinates with the U2 complex to incur an advantageous splicing variant of DDX39B via the suppression of intron retention. Concomitantly, SAP30BP bridges splicing dysregulation and metabolic rewiring by enhancing glycolysis while attenuating mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in T-ALL. Small molecule-mediated targeting of the splicing and metabolic process effectively suppresses aggressive T cell malignancies and confers susceptibility to chemotherapy agents.

papers.abstract: Agonistic antibodies targeting the costimulatory receptor GITR have shown limited clinical efficacy despite a strong preclinical rationale, revealing fundamental limitations of receptor-targeted approaches to TNF superfamily agonism. Here, we show that pharmacologically stabilizing the trimeric structure of human GITRL offers a mechanistically distinct strategy to overcome these limitations. Small-molecule stabilization of GITRL preserves its membrane residency. It enables bidirectional signaling between antigen-presenting cells and T cells, a physiological context that receptor-targeted antibodies bypass through nonphysiological clustering of GITR. In humanized GITR/GITRL double-knock-in mice bearing syngeneic tumors, GITRL stabilization expands cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, reduces intratumoral regulatory T cell frequency, activates APCs, and restructures the immune spatial architecture. In patient-derived tumor explants, GITRL stabilization reactivates suppressed CD8+ T cells in an APC-dependent manner. Our findings establish ligand stabilization as a mechanistically distinct therapeutic strategy and provide a framework for engaging TNF receptor superfamily costimulatory pathways by modulating their native ligands.

papers.abstract: Biological networks with preferential fiber alignment along a particular direction endow tissues with orientation-dependent mechanical properties. The mechanical response of structurally anisotropic fibrous networks to internally generated, spherically symmetric deformation is relevant to tumor expansion; however, it remains poorly understood. Here, we report the experimental results and theoretical studies of this deformation in a model hydrogel with controlled radial or lateral fiber orientation around an expanding spherical droplet. By integrating cavitation rheology with polarized optical microscopy, we found that the effective Young's modulus of the hydrogels exhibits a strong dependence on fiber orientation, increasing with a higher degree of lateral fiber alignment and decreasing with stronger radial alignment. These findings agree with the results of the developed affine model accounting for the mechanical asymmetry of fibrous architectures. Our work provides the basis for understanding similar mechanical responses in structurally anisotropic biological matrices.

papers.abstract: The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis. ASCL1, a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including PRMT5. Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

papers.abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti-breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)-mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell-mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8+ T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti-PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer has the worst prognosis among common solid tumours. Surgical and systemic therapies are too often non-curative, highlighting the need to identify patients with aggressive tumour biology. Here, we molecularly characterize the tumours of short-term and long-term survivors after pancreatic cancer surgery. Whole-exome and RNA-sequenced tumours in the Oncology Research Information Exchange Network (ORIEN) were used to compare patients with short-term survival ( 3 years) survival after surgery, stratified by upfront surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Differentially expressed genes were validated in independent cohorts. 140 patients had upfront surgery (short-term n = 81; long-term n = 59) and 45 patients had neoadjuvant chemotherapy (short-term n = 29; long-term n = 16). Tumours in long-term survivors after upfront surgery were more often of classical subtypes and presented with immune-enriched microenvironment signatures, whereas tumours in short-term survivors were more often basal-like with a fibrotic microenvironment signature. Short-term survivors had enriched gene sets associated with ECM production, stromal fibroblasts and angiogenesis, suggesting influence of the microenvironment composition on prognosis. Of the overexpressed genes in short-term survivors after upfront surgery, high expression levels of S100A2, S100A3, HMGA2, and A2ML1 were validated as prognostic in two independent cohorts. Neoadjuvant therapy was associated with classical subtypes and differences in immune cell proportions. Short-term survival following PDAC surgery is associated with basal-like subtypes and fibrotic microenvironment signatures with EMT activation. Overexpression of S100A2, S100A3, HMGA2, and A2ML1 is associated with short overall survival, and these genes are potential prognostic biomarkers that warrant further validation before use in PDAC surgical and oncological care.

papers.abstract: Despite the success of stool-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening programs, their reliance on patient compliance and variable sensitivity/specificity underscores the need for complementary blood-based biomarkers enabling early and accurate detection. We previously identified oncofetal chondroitin sulfate (ofCS), a tumour-associated glycosaminoglycan broadly expressed as a post-translational modification on proteoglycans across multiple malignancies. This study aimed to identify and evaluate circulating ofCS-modified proteoglycans (ofCSPGs) as potential plasma biomarkers for CRC detection. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic performance of individual circulating ofCSPGs for distinguishing CRC patients from healthy individuals. Secondary endpoints included assessment of the requirement for ofCS modification for cancer-specific detection, and performance of a multimarker panel across disease stages. Plasma samples from CRC patients and healthy donors were analysed in two independent cohorts (n = 64 and n = 176). Levels of seven candidate proteoglycans, including agrin, colony-stimulating factor 1, decorin, endocan, neuropilin-1, syndecan-1, and tenascin-C, were measured using a novel ofCS-capture ELISA based on the high-affinity ofCS-binding reagent rVAR2. Across both cohorts, the ofCSPGs were significantly elevated in CRC plasma compared with healthy controls (p < .01). Notably, the ofCS modification was required for cancer-specific detection of neuropilin-1, syndecan-1, and tenascin-C. A combined panel of colony-stimulating factor 1 and syndecan-1 demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for CRC detection, distinguishing CRC patients from controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of .96. Performance was maintained across disease stages. Plasma ofCS-modified proteoglycans represent a promising class of blood-based biomarkers for CRC detection. These findings support further clinical development of ofCSPG-based assays as complementary tools for CRC screening and early diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Preoperative anxiety and venipuncture-related distress are common in preschool children undergoing day-case surgery. Intranasal dexmedetomidine provides respiratory-sparing sedation, but the proportion meeting prespecified venipuncture sedation criteria with monotherapy is variable. To determine whether buccal esketamine added to intranasal dexmedetomidine improves procedural sedation success during pre-induction venipuncture. In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 168 children aged 2-6 years undergoing elective day-case surgery were randomized to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine plus buccal esketamine 0.5 mg/kg or buccal placebo. Age-stratified block randomization and concealed allocation were used. The primary endpoint required University of Michigan Sedation Scale (UMSS) ≥ 2 within 40 min, followed by successful venipuncture 10 min after the qualifying assessment, with UMSS ≥ 2 and a venipuncture behavior score of 1-2 at puncture. Analyses included intention-to-treat, per-protocol, adjusted, and extreme-case sensitivity analyses. In the intention-to-treat population, procedural sedation success was higher with the combination than with dexmedetomidine alone (53/84 [63.1%] vs. 36/84 [42.9%]; absolute risk difference, 20.2 percentage points; OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.23-4.23; p = 0.009; number needed to treat 5). The per-protocol analysis was consistent (53/82 [64.6%] vs. 36/83 [43.4%]; OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.27-4.47; p = 0.007). Venipuncture succeeded at the first attempt in all 165 children who underwent it. Median sedation onset did not differ (26.0 vs. 24.5 min; p = 0.339). No episode meeting the prespecified definition of clinically important oversedation was occurred. Bradycardia occurred in four children (4.8%) with dexmedetomidine alone and in none with the combination. In preschool children undergoing day-case surgery, adding buccal esketamine 0.5 mg/kg to intranasal dexmedetomidine increased the proportion meeting prespecified procedural sedation success criteria during venipuncture. This trial supports a monitored multimodal premedication strategy within a defined pathway and warrants further evaluation of dose, pharmacokinetics, and safety. The Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400084040); date of registration: 9 May 2024.

papers.abstract: Gastric signet-ring cell carcinoma (GSRCC) frequently exhibits peritoneal dissemination and chemotherapy resistance. This study investigated the contribution of ZDHHC7-dependent MYH9 S-palmitoylation to GSRCC progression and oxaliplatin resistance. ZDHHC7 expression and clinical associations were assessed using public transcriptomic datasets and patient specimens. Functional studies were conducted in GSRCC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and mouse models. Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation identified and validated ZDHHC7-associated proteins. Acyl-biotin exchange, click chemistry-based labeling, mutagenesis, subcellular fractionation, and immunofluorescence assessed MYH9 S-palmitoylation and localization. PI3K signaling was examined through phosphorylation measurements and pharmacological modulation. Statistical analyses included Student's t-tests, analysis of variance, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank tests. ZDHHC7 was upregulated in GSRCC, and higher expression was associated with advanced TNM stage and poorer survival. ZDHHC7 depletion reduced clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion, increased apoptosis, impaired organoid growth, reduced peritoneal tumor burden, and increased oxaliplatin sensitivity. ZDHHC7 associated with MYH9 and regulated its S-palmitoylation, with Cys172 identified as a major modification site. Wild-type ZDHHC7, but not the catalytically inactive C160S mutant, restored MYH9 plasma membrane enrichment in ZDHHC7-deficient cells. Compared with wild-type MYH9, the C172S mutant exhibited reduced S-palmitoylation and plasma membrane localization, accompanied by decreased PI3K-Akt phosphorylation. MYH9 depletion prevented ZDHHC7 overexpression from enhancing pathway phosphorylation. Pharmacological PI3K activation attenuated the effects of ZDHHC7 depletion, whereas inhibition increased oxaliplatin sensitivity. In mice, reconstitution with MYH9-C172S reduced peritoneal tumor burden, metastatic nodules, and ascites and increased oxaliplatin responsiveness compared with wild-type MYH9. ZDHHC7-dependent MYH9 S-palmitoylation at Cys172 contributes to GSRCC progression and oxaliplatin resistance. Disrupting this modification reduces MYH9 membrane localization, attenuates PI3K-Akt signaling, and suppresses peritoneal tumor growth, providing a preclinical basis for investigating this regulatory axis as a therapeutic target. ZDHHC7 is preferentially upregulated in GSRCC and associated with poorer patient survival. ZDHHC7-dependent MYH9 Cys172 palmitoylation is linked to membrane association and PI3K-Akt signalling. Disruption of MYH9 Cys172 palmitoylation reduces peritoneal tumour burden and increases oxaliplatin responsiveness in experimental models.

papers.abstract: Cancer progression is fundamentally driven by oncogenic mutations and dynamic remodelling of the tumour mechanical microenvironment. Accumulating evidence suggests that the biomechanical properties of the tumour mechanical microenvironment such as stiffness of extracellular matrix (ECM), viscoelasticity, interstitial fluid pressure (IFP) and solid stress are abnormally altered. Such properties considerably influence various aspects of cancer progression, including proliferation, migration, metabolism and treatment resistance. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of how the tumour mechanical microenvironment regulates cancer progression is crucial for precise cancer diagnosis and treatment. In this review, we examine in detail the biomechanical properties of the tumour mechanical microenvironment, focusing particularly on how these properties critically influence cancer progression. Finally, we discuss strategies to achieve clinical benefits through modulating matrix abnormalities, regulating mechanical signal transduction and enhancing drug delivery. The tumour mechanical microenvironment is not only a contributing factor to cancer progression but also a new direction for targeted therapy. The tumour mechanical microenvironment is a dynamic and complex ecosystem comprising multiple biomechanical properties. The tumour mechanical microenvironment profoundly influences the proliferation, metastasis, metabolism, angiogenesis, drug resistance and immune escape of tumours. Modulating tumour mechanical microenvironments, rather than merely destroying tumour cells, may be an effective therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to identify sociodemographic, clinical, and health system factors associated with attendance at a cancer genetic appointment following referral. Retrospective electronic health record study of adults referred to the MaineHealth Cancer Risk and Prevention Clinic for cancer genetic counseling from January 1, 2017, through December 31, 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with appointment attendance. Exposures included sociodemographic factors (age, sex, race, primary language, rurality, area deprivation index [ADI], insurance status), clinical characteristics (cancer history, non-cancer comorbidity burden), and referral characteristics (source, urgency, number of referrals). Among 10,589 referred individuals (median [IQR] age, 53 [39-65] years; 83% female), 6555 (62%) were scheduled and 5933 (56%) attended; most attrition occurred before scheduling with 91% of scheduled individuals attending their appointment. In multivariable analysis, lower odds of attendance were observed among those that were male (OR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.65-0.80]), non-White (OR, 0.59 [95% CI, 0.49-0.71]), non-English-speaking (OR, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.25-0.49]), residing in high-ADI areas (OR, 0.85 [95% CI, 0.77-0.93]), covered by government insurance (OR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.76-0.91]), self-pay status (OR, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.45-0.67]), those with greater non-cancer comorbidity burden (OR per condition, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.78-0.95]) and those receiving more than 1 referral (OR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.69-0.93]). Older age (> 53 years) (OR, 1.17 [95% CI, 1.07-1.28]), cancer history (OR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.29-1.58]), and urgent referral classification (OR, 3.77 [95% CI, 3.23-4.40]) were associated with higher odds of attendance. Nearly half of the cohort did not complete an appointment. Completion was associated with sociodemographic, clinical, and workflow factors, highlighting barriers affecting equitable access to precision oncology services.

papers.abstract: Aberrant sialoglycosylation is a hallmark of gastric cancer (GC) and has been implicated in tumour progression, immune evasion and metastasis. Among the most clinically relevant sialoglycans are sialyl-Tn (sTn) and sialyl-Lewis a (sLeA), yet their prognostic value, molecular context and functional protein carriers remain incompletely understood. Here, we analysed sTn and sLeA expression in over 200 clinically annotated GC cases, including primary tumours and matched metastases using immunohistochemistry, proximity ligation assays and lectin-enrichment glycoproteomics. Both antigens were frequently co-expressed within tumour areas and maintained in metastatic lesions. While glycan alone was not an independent predictor of outcome, their combined overexpression defined a clinically aggressive subgroup with significantly reduced survival. Importantly, the dual sTn/sLeA signature provided complementary prognostic stratification within established The Cancer Genome Atlas molecular subtypes. This effect was particularly evident among microsatellite-instable tumours. Glycoproteomic enrichment, spatial proximity assays and CEACAM5 immunoprecipitation prioritised CEACAM5 as a tumour-associated candidate carrier, with strongest support for CEACAM5-associated immature O-glycosylation consistent with sTn. CEACAM5 expression correlated with advanced disease and poor survival, remaining an independent prognostic factor in multivariate analysis. Functional studies in CRISPR-engineered GC cells supported a contribution of CEACAM5 to invasion in a context of immature O-glycosylation. Collectively, these findings define a clinically relevant sialoglycan signature that refines molecular classification and patient risk assessment in GC. Moreover, they nominate CEACAM5-associated sialoglycosylation as a candidate biomarker axis for identifying aggressive GC and guiding future glycoform-directed strategies. Dual sTn/sLeA overexpression defines a high-risk gastric cancer subgroup. The sTn/sLeA signature refines prognosis within TCGA molecular subtypes. Integrated glycoproteomic and proximity-based analyses prioritize CEACAM5 as a candidate sialoglycan carrier. CEACAM5 contributes to invasion in an immature O-glycosylation context and independently predicts poor outcome.

papers.abstract: Traditional biomarkers (e.g., programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), tumor mutational burden (TMB), deficient mismatch repair (dMMR), and microsatellite instability (MSI)) are limited by spatiotemporal heterogeneity and insufficient tumor-immune interactions, leading to suboptimal treatment efficacy prediction. Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) and immune co-culture models partially mitigated these limitations by mimicking tumor biology. This review systematically summarizes the construction strategies of PDTOs and the advantages and limitations of different tumor organoid-immune co-culture models. It further explores the applications of microfluidic technology, 3D bioprinting technology, and organ-on-a-chip technology in constructing a more biomimetic tumor organoid-immune co-culture system. In addition, the review outlines the systematic evaluation scheme for tumor organoid-immune co-cultures. Meanwhile, the review evaluates the performance of tumor organoid-immune co-culture models in drug sensitivity testing, prediction of immunotherapy responses, and evaluation of cell therapies. Cell/tissue source heterogeneity impacts model success rates. Native models (such as air-liquid interface culture models and patient-derived organotypic tumor spheroids) and reconstituted models (such as tumor sphere models) can simulate the tumor immune microenvironment and support the complex interactions between immune cells and tumor cells. Selection depends on tumor origin for more accurate simulation. These models show promise in evaluating immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T/NK therapies, and chemotherapy-immunotherapy combinations via integrated detection methods (flow cytometry, imaging, cytokine profiling). PDTOs retain selected histological and genomic features of the sampled tumor to a certain extent. When combined with immune components, they provide an experimental approach for personalized and precise immunotherapy. However, their clinical predictive utility requires further validation in larger prospective studies.

papers.abstract: KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) exhibits marked molecular and clinical heterogeneity. However, most evidence derives from Western populations, where KRAS G12C predominates. The clinical relevance of major KRAS subtypes and their co-mutation patterns in Asian patients remains incompletely defined. We retrospectively analyzed 171 patients with advanced KRAS-mutant NSCLC treated at two institutions in Korea. Clinical characteristics, PD-L1 expression, treatment outcomes, and genomic alterations were evaluated. Genomic profiles and co-occurring mutations were compared among KRAS G12C, G12D, and G12V subtypes, with a focus on overall survival (OS) and immunotherapy outcomes. KRAS G12C, G12D, and G12V subtypes occurred at similar frequencies. G12C tumors were associated with male sex and smoking history, whereas G12V tumors were more common in females and never-smokers. G12D tumors showed intermediate clinical features. PD-L1 expression tended to be higher in G12C and G12V tumors. Distinct co-mutation patterns were observed: G12C tumors frequently harbored DNA damage response alterations, including ATM and CHEK2, often with STK11 or KEAP1 mutations. G12D tumors exhibited relatively sparse co-mutations, while G12V tumors commonly showed concurrent KEAP1-STK11 alterations. OS following immunotherapy did not differ significantly by KRAS subtype. TP53 mutation was associated with improved outcomes at the cohort level, whereas KEAP1-STK11 co-alterations were associated with poorer survival; these associations were not uniform across KRAS subtypes and subgroup sizes were small. In this Asian cohort, KRAS-mutant NSCLC demonstrates subtype-specific clinical and genomic characteristics. Co-mutation status may add context beyond KRAS subtype alone when interpreting immunotherapy outcomes, but this observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Intramuscular myxoma (IM) is a rare benign mesenchymal tumor with incompletely understood molecular pathogenesis. While GNAS mutations are a known driver, secondary alterations and drivers of GNAS-wildtype cases remain unexplored. Herein, we perform the first integrated clinicopathological, genomic, and epigenomic analysis of a large IM cohort. A total of 34 patients were reviewed, including 12 men and 22 women, with median age of 59 years (range 25-73 years) and tumor size of 5.75 cm (range 2-26.4 cm). Whole exome sequencing performed in 29 cases identified activating GNAS mutation in 65.5% (19/29) cases, predominantly R201C (9/19) and R201H (9/19), and rarely R201S (1/19). TRAF7 was the most common secondary genetic alteration, co-occurring exclusively with GNAS mutation, but there were no significant clinicopathological differences with respect to TRAF7 mutation status. GNAS-wildtype tumors (10/29; 34.5%) exhibited a significantly elevated fraction of genome altered (FGA), with a subset featuring widespread loss of heterozygosity (LOH) and recurrent NF1 inactivating mutations leading to its biallelic inactivation (n = 3). The histology of these cases demonstrated increased vascularity with interconnecting and staghorn vessels and some featured perivascular hyalinization. No significant clinicopathological differences were observed between GNAS mutated and wildtype cases. Dimensionality reduction analysis and unsupervised hierarchical clustering of DNA methylation profiles (n = 22) demonstrated that all IM cases formed a distinct cluster separate from other mesenchymal tumors, with further subclustering by GNAS status. Methylation-based sarcoma classifier (v13.1) showed only modest diagnostic concordance with overall accuracy of 36.4%. Our findings demonstrated that IM encompasses two molecularly distinct subtypes defined by GNAS mutation status, with GNAS-wildtype cases showing profound genomic instability. A subset harbored near-haploidy with biallelic NF1 inactivation, which closely resembled the recently described distinctive near-haploid fibromyxoid neoplasm (DNHFN). Given the overlap in histology, genome-wide LOH and methylation profile, DNHFN may represent a subtype of GNAS-wildtype intramuscular myxoma. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) carcinoma is a rare, highly aggressive cancer driven by NUTM1 rearrangements and typically arises in the midline structures. Prognosis is poor, and emerging evidence suggests primary tumor sites influence outcomes. This study compares overall and cancer-specific survival among adults with NUT carcinoma in the nasal cavity/paranasal sinuses (NUT NCS) with lung/bronchus (NUT LB). This retrospective cohort study used the SEER database with histologically confirmed NUT carcinoma. Patients were categorized by primary site (NCS vs. LB). Covariates included age, sex, and stage at diagnosis. Survival outcomes were analyzed by using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression. Of 127 patients, 77 had LB and 50 had NCS primaries. LB tumors were more common in younger patients (55.8% aged 19-49 vs. 38.0%; p = 0.009). NCS tumors more frequently presented with T4 disease (76% vs. 53.3%; p = 0.030), whereas LB tumors more frequently exhibited N1-N3 nodal disease (71.5% vs. 30%; p < 0.001) and distant metastasis (53.3% vs. 16%; p < 0.001). Unadjusted survival did not differ by site. In multivariable analysis, LB showed a higher overall mortality (HR 1.84, 95% CI 1.07-3.16) and cancer-specific mortality (HR 2.10, 95% CI 1.14-3.89). Pulmonary NUT carcinoma showed more disseminated disease and worse adjusted survival than NCS. Primary site appears prognostically relevant, although findings are limited by registry constraints and treatment confounding.

papers.abstract: The increasing use of neoadjuvant systemic therapy (NAST) has altered breast cancer management. Although NAST can downstage axillary disease, some patients with clinically node-negative disease harbor occult nodal metastases. This study sought to evaluate the rate of pathologic lymph node positivity in clinically node-negative patients after NAST and identify predictors of nodal status. This retrospective cohort study utilized National Cancer Database (NCDB) data from 2018 to 2023 for patients with stage I-III cN0 breast cancer who received NAST and underwent definitive breast and axillary surgery. Pathologic lymph node positivity was the primary outcome, stratified by receptor subtype and breast pathologic complete response (pCR), defined as the absence of residual invasive disease in the breast. Of 54,874 cN0 patients, 13.4% had pathologic node positivity. Nodal positivity varied significantly across receptor subtypes (p < 0.001), with estrogen receptor/progesterone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative tumors demonstrating the highest rate (33.2%). Achieving breast pCR was strongly associated with negative nodal disease; 2% of patients with breast pCR and 21% of those without breast pCR had positive nodes (p < 0.0001). Multivariable analysis confirmed that receptor subtype and breast pCR were independently associated with nodal status. Pathologic nodal positivity after NAST is strongly dictated by receptor subtype. Our findings suggest that, for specific receptor subtypes, the routine use of intraoperative frozen section analysis may be unnecessary, potentially reducing operative delays and costs. These results support a biology-driven approach to axillary management that optimizes both surgical efficiency and patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: Pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) is a promising strategy for patients with unresectable peritoneal metastases (PM). Globally, as healthcare systems increasingly adopt value-based care, there is a growing need to evaluate patient-centered outcomes and costs of emerging technologies. We evaluated health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and healthcare costs following consecutive PIPAC procedures in patients with unresectable PM. We prospectively recruited patients with unresectable PM from various primary origins for PIPAC with oxaliplatin or doxorubicin/cisplatin between August 2020 and July 2023. HRQoL was assessed using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General (FACT-G) and EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level. Cumulative and period-specific costs in Singapore dollars (S$, based on the average 2023 World Bank exchange rate, 1 USD = 1.34 Singapore dollars) were examined using hospital billing records. Linear mixed-effects regression models were used to evaluate longitudinal changes in HRQoL. A total of 42 patients underwent 84 PIPACs. HRQoL was maintained throughout repeated PIPACs without significant periprocedural deterioration. Among patients completing three PIPACs, though FACT-G total scores improved (change = 6.0, 95% CI - 10.5 to 22.5), this did not reach statistical significance. Mean cumulative cost per patient was S$46,308 (standard deviation [SD] S$21,058). Mean PIPAC period-specific cost was S$23,154 (SD S$14,546); 64% was attributable to PIPAC admission, 18% to outpatient services, and 18% to emergency visits and readmissions. For each PIPAC admission, 35% of the cost was attributable to surgery, 28% to ward stay, and 1% to drugs. Repeated PIPAC maintained HRQoL without periprocedural deterioration in patients with unresectable PM, supporting its role as a palliative treatment strategy. Surgery-related costs accounted for 35% of total healthcare expenditure.

papers.abstract: Tigilanol tiglate (TT) is a small molecule under development for the treatment of solid tumours. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that intralesional injection of TT leads to rapid ablation of injected tumours via a multifactorial mode of action that incorporates vasculature disruption, pro-inflammatory cytokine production, tumour cell pyroptosis and release of damage-associated molecular patterns; characteristics of immunogenic cell death (ICD). T cell infiltration into murine tumours has also been observed following TT treatment, with improved responses to immunotherapy. We assessed immune cell infiltration and markers of ICD in tumours following TT administration in biopsies taken as part of a Phase Ib/IIa clinical trial in human head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) patients. A total of 19 patients were treated in two cohorts. Pre-treatment biopsies were taken 7 days prior to treatment. Post-treatment biopsies were taken 1, 8 or 24 h following treatment, and at tumour excision between 14 and 21 days after treatment. We demonstrate significant CD8+ and CD68+cells suggestive of T cell and monocyte/macrophage infiltration 14-21 days following TT treatment (n = 11), as well as the presence of tertiary lymphoid structure-like aggregates in a subset (n = 4) of patient tumours. Consistent with our preclinical findings, we show loss of nuclear HMGB1 staining, increased phosphorylation of eIF-2α, and calreticulin externalisation in tumour cells following treatment (n = 4), suggesting TT may induce ICD in HNSCC patients. These findings support the preclinical data and demonstrate TT treatment induces immune cell recruitment to HNSCC tumours, with the potential to combine with immunotherapy for improved patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: Trophoblast cell-surface antigen-2 (Trop-2) is a transmembrane glycoprotein widely overexpressed in epithelial cancers and implicated in tumor growth, survival, invasion, and metastasis. Trop-2 acts as a calcium signal transducer, promoting cancer cell proliferation, migration, and survival through pathways such as PI3K/AKT and MAPK. Its differential expression in tumor and normal tissues has enabled the development of Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). To date, sacituzumab govitecan-which delivers the topoisomerase I inhibitor SN-38 (active irinotecan metabolite)-has received regulatory approval for advanced breast cancer. Datopotamab deruxtecan-which carries a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor (deruxtecan)-has more recently also gained approval in select settings of refractory breast cancer and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. Regulatory approval of these ADCs has relied on proof of efficacy in refractory disease, durability of response, and a manageable safety profile, including characterization of class-specific toxicities such as neutropenia, diarrhea, stomatitis, and interstitial lung disease. Notably, current approvals do not require Trop-2 biomarker selection; enrollment in pivotal trials was largely unselected, reflecting the high prevalence of Trop-2 expression across tumor types. However, variability in expression and emerging resistance mechanisms highlight the need for refined patient stratification. Ongoing studies are evaluating next-generation Trop-2 ADCs, other ways of targeting Trop-2, the role of biomarkers, and combination strategies. The role of Trop-2-targeted therapies as a pan-cancer approach needs to be further evaluated.

papers.abstract: The complex interactions between tumors and microbes within the tumor-microbe microenvironment (TMME) are increasingly recognized as critical determinants of tumor progression and therapeutic response. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the presence of intratumoral microbes (ITMs), their routes of entry into tumors, and their functional roles within the TMME, and highlights emerging TMME-targeted strategies for diagnosis and treatment of tumors with ITMs. ITMs can profoundly influence tumor biology by modulating cellular signaling and immune responses, with consequent changes in therapeutic efficacy. For instance, Fusobacterium nucleatum impairs CD8+ T-cell infiltration via succinic acid in drug-resistant colorectal cancer, while cytidine deaminase-expressing bacteria inactivate gemcitabine in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. We summarize the defining characteristics of the TMME, including hypoxia, acidity, and oxidative stress, as well as microbial-associated features such as biofilm formation, bacterial enzymes, and metabolite production. These factors collectively contribute to a dynamic ecosystem that supports microbial persistence and impacts tumor development, immune regulation, and treatment outcomes. Current therapeutic strategies targeting ITM tumors are critically evaluated, including microbial modulation approaches, non-antibiotic modalities, and nanomedicine-based co-delivery systems that combine antibiotics with chemotherapeutics. Co-delivery systems, such as a liposome platform that delivers ciprofloxacin and gemcitabine, allow simultaneous targeting of tumor cells and intratumoral microbes by exploiting the acidic, hypoxic, and enzyme- and metabolite-rich features of the TMME. This TMME-responsive design allows site-specific drug release while eliminating ITMs, and thereby overcomes microbe-induced chemoresistance and enhances therapeutic efficacy. Finally, we highlight the opportunities and challenges associated with TMME-targeted interventions. While modulation or elimination of tumor-associated microbes represents a promising strategy for improving treatment outcomes, significant barriers remain, including a lack of standardized diagnostic tools, microbial heterogeneity, safety concerns, and limited mechanistic understanding of tumor-microbe interactions. Advances in this field will require integrated multi-omics approaches and better translational models for the development of precise, personalized therapies for ITM tumors.

papers.abstract: Retinoblastoma (RB) is the most common childhood intraocular malignancy. RB1 germline variants predispose to early-onset bilateral disease, but associations with treatment response and post-treatment ocular outcomes are incompletely characterized. Retrospective cohort study of 120 intraocular RB patients treated at Children's Hospital Affiliated to Shandong University (2016-2021). Patients were stratified into carriers (n = 41; pathogenic/likely pathogenic RB1 germline variants) and non-carriers (n = 79). Eye-level generalized estimating equations (GEE) evaluated treatment response and post-treatment outcomes, adjusting for International Intraocular Retinoblastoma Classification (IIRC) stage, laterality, age, sex, and five separately entered treatment modalities (intravenous, intra-arterial, and intravitreal chemotherapy; laser photocoagulation; cryotherapy). Carriers presented younger, with more bilateral disease and multifocal disease. At the eye level, non-carrier eyes showed higher proportions of IIRC Group D/E (83.3% vs. 55.2%, p < 0.001) and mixed growth pattern (41.7% vs. 16.4%, p = 0.001), while carrier eyes had a higher proportion of endophytic pattern (71.6% vs. 54.8%, p = 0.043). On eye-level GEE analysis, RB1 variant status was associated with post-treatment cataract (adjusted OR = 3.42, 95% CI 1.13-10.30, p = 0.029). Post-treatment phthisis bulbi occurred exclusively in carrier eyes (4/67 vs. 0/84, p = 0.037). At the eye level, RB1 variant status was associated with distinct IIRC stage distribution and growth patterns, and with post-treatment cataract after adjusting for five separately entered treatment modalities-though this cataract finding should be considered hypothesis-generating given the absence of detailed treatment dose data. These findings suggest a potential role for RB1 pathway dysfunction in ocular tissue vulnerability beyond tumor suppression, warranting prospective validation.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between JAM3/PAX1 methylation and cervical lesion severity and assess its diagnostic performance, alone and in combination with HPV16/18 genotyping, for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher (CIN2+) in hrHPV-positive women. A total of 205 treatment-negative hrHPV-positive women with available JAM3/PAX1 methylation results and histopathological diagnoses were included in this hospital-based study. The association between methylation positivity and cervical lesion severity was evaluated using the Cochran-Armitage trend test. A subset of 105 participants with complete HPV genotyping, cytology, methylation, and histopathological data was further analyzed using ordinal logistic regression and diagnostic performance measures, including sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Among the 205 participants, JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity increased with cervical lesion severity, with positivity rates of 20.00% in the normal group, 23.53% in CIN1, 33.33% in CIN2, 61.43% in CIN3, and 65.12% in cervical cancer (P for trend < 0.001). In the complete-data subset (n = 105), JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity (OR = 5.02, 95% CI: 2.15-11.77) and HPV16/18 positivity (OR = 3.88, 95% CI: 1.75-8.60) were independently associated with higher cervical lesion grades. Parallel testing of JAM3/PAX1 methylation and HPV16/18 genotyping achieved a sensitivity of 86.81% and a specificity of 50.00% for CIN2+ detection, whereas sequential testing yielded a sensitivity of 43.96% and a specificity of 92.86%. JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity was associated with cervical lesion severity in hrHPV-positive women. Combining JAM3/PAX1 methylation with HPV16/18 genotyping provided different sensitivity-specificity trade-offs for CIN2+ detection. These findings suggest that JAM3/PAX1 methylation may serve as an adjunctive marker for cervical lesion risk assessment, although further validation in larger and less-selected screening populations is needed.

papers.abstract: Heart and lung exposure are often discussed together in breast radiotherapy, although their doses may arise from different constraints. We tested whether contemporary breast radiotherapy is characterized by organ-specific dose-generating mechanisms rather than a common determinant structure. This retrospective study included 276 women with unilateral breast cancer treated with intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) or volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) from January 2022 through June 2023. Mean heart dose (Heart Dmean) and ipsilateral lung mean dose (Lung Dmean) were modeled using multivariable ordinary least-squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors. Four-degree-of-freedom B-splines assessed nonlinear planning-target-volume (PTV) effects. Organ-by-factor interactions were examined in a joint standardized mixed model. Maximum heart distance (MHD) was evaluated in left-sided cases. Sensitivity analyses included Gamma generalized linear models and exclusion of deep-inspiration breath-hold cases. Exploratory Shapley/LMG decomposition quantified each predictor group's share of model-explained variance. Left-sided disease was the dominant determinant of Heart Dmean (+217.38 cGy; 95% CI, 184.59-250.18; P<.001), whereas regional nodal irradiation (RNI) was the strongest determinant of Lung Dmean (+271.30 cGy; 95% CI, 182.52-360.07; P<.001). PTV volume showed a nonlinear association with Lung Dmean (joint spline P<.001) but not Heart Dmean (P = .119). VMAT was associated with lower Lung Dmean (-93.05 cGy; P = .011) without a corresponding Heart Dmean difference. The joint model confirmed organ-specific effects for laterality, RNI, and technique. Among 128 left-sided patients, MHD was not associated with Heart Dmean (Spearman ρ=.071; P = .424). Shapley/LMG decomposition attributed 81.9% of explained Heart Dmean variance to laterality, whereas RNI contributed the largest share for Lung Dmean (35.4%). Cardiac and ipsilateral lung dose followed different constraint hierarchies: anatomy dominated cardiac exposure, while treatment extent and target geometry dominated lung exposure. Organ-specific models may therefore be more useful than generic normal-tissue risk frameworks for individualized breast radiotherapy planning.

papers.abstract: Over-biopsy in prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis significantly increases patient morbidity and healthcare costs, underscoring the urgent need for more precise noninvasive tools to guide biopsy decisions. This prospective study analyzed pre-biopsy urine samples from 473 patients using DNA methylation profiling. The urinary tumor-associated DNA methylation assay exhibited high diagnostic accuracy for PCa, achieving the area under receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.965 (84.48% sensitivity, 96.40% specificity) in the training cohort and 0.938 (84.21% sensitivity, 98.04% specificity) in an independent validation cohort. The assay also showed strong performance in detecting clinically significant PCa (csPCa, Gleason score ≥ 7), with AUCs of 0.948 and 0.913, respectively. A novel multidimensional model that incorporated PSA levels, multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) features, and methylation signatures further enhanced diagnostic precision, yielding AUCs of 0.985 for PCa and 0.971 for csPCa. Clinically, this model could reduce unnecessary biopsies by 42.9% while missing only 3.9% of csPCa cases. Importantly, the assay performed consistently well across the full PSA spectrum. Its strong predictive performance supported the initiation of a pilot clinical trial, providing initial evidence for its application in biopsy-free diagnosis. The urinary DNA methylation assay represents a promising development in PCa diagnostics. By synergistically combining PSA levels, mpMRI findings, and methylation patterns, this innovative multidimensional model achieves superior diagnostic accuracy while substantially reducing unnecessary biopsies, though further external and prospective validation studies are warranted to fully establish its clinical utility.

papers.abstract: CAR T-cell therapy has demonstrated improved efficacy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma compared with standard systemic treatments. However, there are no datasets evaluating BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy in solid organ transplant recipients with multiple myeloma, and whether the immunosuppressants these patients receive interfere with CAR T-cell efficacy. Here we present the first report of a kidney transplant recipient with relapsed multiple myeloma successfully treated with CAR T-cell therapy without compromising product efficacy or allograft function. We describe how immunosuppressant therapy was managed, providing a preliminary blueprint for effective CAR T-cell use in this complex patient population. Additionally, using peripheral blood samples banked throughout the treatment course, we performed ex vivo immune profiling showing minimal effects of immunosuppressives on circulating CAR T-cells as their doses were adjusted.

papers.abstract: Primary renal tumors vary in their proximity to organs at risk (OARs), particularly the gastrointestinal tract. This prospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and local control of stereotactic MR-guided adaptive radiotherapy (SMART) with prospectively permitted OAR-constrained dose de-escalation. This single-institution phase II trial enrolled patients with a T1N0M0 primary renal tumor ≤5 cm who were ineligible for or declined surgery or ablation. Baseline renal function was not an exclusion criterion. SMART was delivered on an MR-linac (Elekta Unity) at 42 Gy in 3 fractions, reduced in 3 Gy steps (minimum, 30 Gy) if OAR constraints could not be met. The co-primary endpoints were the 1-year local control rate and the rate of serious adverse events (grade ≥3, excluding nephrotoxicity). Twenty-five patients were enrolled between May 2022 and December 2024 (median age, 79 years; median tumor diameter, 22 mm); no spacer was used. Prescribed doses were 42 Gy in 22 patients, 36 Gy in 1, and 30 Gy in 2; all patients completed 3 fractions. With a median follow-up of 22.1 months, no local or distant recurrence was observed; one patient died of an unrelated cause. The 1-year local control rate was 100% (95% CI, 86.3%-100%). One serious adverse event occurred (4%; 95% CI, 0.1%-20.4%; grade 3 myocardial infarction, judged unrelated to SMART). In 22 patients evaluable for renal function, the median change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was -7.5 mL/min/1.73 m² (interquartile range, -10.0 to -4.2); one additional patient with baseline eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m² initiated dialysis at 4 months. SMART was feasible, with encouraging short-term local control and no treatment-related serious adverse events excluding nephrotoxicity. Daily OAR-constrained dose modulation may allow treatment of OAR-adjacent tumors previously considered unsuitable for stereotactic body radiotherapy. Longer follow-up and multicenter studies are warranted.

papers.abstract: Recurrence remains a major concern following resection of World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 meningiomas. Identification of preoperative factors associated with recurrence may improve risk stratification and inform postoperative surveillance and treatment strategies. We sought to identify clinical and radiographic predictors of recurrence-free survival (RFS) in patients with WHO grade 2 meningiomas. We retrospectively analyzed adults undergoing resection of intracranial WHO grade 2 meningiomas from 2010 to 2023. Clinical, radiographic, surgical, and treatment-related variables were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression. Preoperative tumor burden was estimated volumetrically using an ellipsoid-based method. The multivariable model included preoperative tumor volume, Simpson grade, skull base location, and planned adjuvant radiotherapy (RT). Alternative measures of surgical outcome were assessed in sensitivity analyses. Among 136 surgical episodes, 38 recurrences occurred. Median preoperative tumor volume was 28.5 cm³. On univariable analysis, greater preoperative tumor volume was associated with worse RFS (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.11-2.10; p = 0.010) and remained independently associated with RFS after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.47, 95% CI 1.05-2.05; p = 0.024). Recurrence occurred in 15.6%, 23.9%, and 44.4% of small-, intermediate-, and large-volume tertiles, respectively (log-rank p = 0.0048). Simpson grade showed a borderline association with RFS, while skull base location and planned RT were not independently associated with RFS. Among evaluated clinical, radiographic, and treatment-related factors, preoperative tumor burden emerged as an independent predictor of RFS in WHO grade 2 meningiomas. Preoperative volumetric assessment may provide a readily available imaging marker to improve recurrence risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Myxopapillary ependymomas (MPEs) are rare spinal ependymal tumors with propensity for local recurrence and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dissemination. While gross-total resection (GTR) is the cornerstone of treatment, the independent contributions of surgical technique and adjuvant radiation therapy (RT) to long-term outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with MPE according to extent of resection (EOR), surgical technique, and adjuvant RT. A retrospective analysis was conducted of patients with MPE who underwent surgical resection at a single institution. Clinical, imaging, and operative variables were collected. Patients were stratified by EOR, surgical technique, and adjuvant RT77-4567890-=/*-. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess PFS. A total of 63 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 54 months. GTR was achieved in 79% of patients, and subtotal resection (STR) was independently associated with worse PFS (p = 0.005). In Kaplan-Meier analysis, PFS did not differ significantly between en-bloc GTR and piecemeal GTR (p = 0.2). Adjuvant RT at doses > = 50.4 Gy was associated with improved PFS in selected higher-risk patients, with the clearest benefit observed after STR, but no measurable benefit after GTR (p = 0.61). Postoperative functional outcomes were favorable, with 80% of evaluable patients maintaining a Frankel D-E status at two years. STR was the strongest predictor of recurrence in MPE, whereas GTR was associated with improved PFS. Although no statistically significant difference in PFS was detected between en bloc and piecemeal GTR, the limited number of recurrence events precludes definitive conclusions regarding their comparative oncological outcomes. En bloc resection remains a desirable goal when safely feasible to preserve capsular integrity. Adjuvant RT may improve PFS after STR, while its role after GTR, including piecemeal GTR, remains uncertain. Future studies should focus on intraoperative predictors of en bloc feasibility and optimize patient selection for adjuvant therapy.

papers.abstract: Primary brain tumors are associated with widespread neuropathology, extending beyond the lesion itself and reflecting the broader impact of disease and treatment-related burden, but distributed structural injury is difficult to quantify across heterogeneous samples. We applied normative modeling to characterize these impacts, capturing how individual regional brain structure deviates from expectations on an individual basis across the adult lifespan in patients with primary brain tumors. We studied 90 adults with primary brain tumors. Cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were converted to age- and sex-adjusted z-scores using CentileBrain normative models after manual censoring of tumor, edema, and resection cavities. Cortical and subcortical burden indices were derived as the sum of regions with z < - 1. We related burden indices to clinical variables, lesion size, seizure history, anti-seizure medication, and corticosteroids, as well as to neuropsychological domain composite scores, with multivariable and hierarchical models accounting for age, sex, and lesion size. Cortical burden was higher in patients with larger tumors, seizure history, and corticosteroid use. After age, sex, and lesion size adjustment, steroids remained associated with cortical burden. Greater cortical burden was associated with poorer processing speed and language, while greater subcortical burden was associated with poorer motor performance. Pre-radiotherapy normative burden in non-lesional tissue captures clinically linked distributed atrophy in adults with primary brain tumors. Lesion size and corticosteroid exposure were the most robust clinical correlates of cortical burden, likely indexing not only drug effects, but also greater disease- and edema-related burden that is not fully captured by lesion size or tumor grade. Domain-specific cognitive associations support burden as a candidate marker of structural and functional vulnerability entering radiotherapy. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is increasingly used to de-escalate axillary surgery in patients with breast cancer with axillary downstaging. Evidence supporting blue dye-only mapping with Patent Blue V remains limited, particularly in resource-limited settings. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included women with invasive breast cancer treated at three public hospitals within the Brazilian Unified Health System between 2017 and 2021. Eligible patients received NAC, converted to clinically node-negative status (ycN0), and underwent definitive breast and axillary surgery. The primary analysis compared patients with initially node-positive disease (cN1-cN2) converted to ycN0 who underwent Patent Blue V-only SLNB or axillary lymph node dissection (ALND). The primary endpoint was axillary recurrence. Secondary endpoints included locoregional recurrence, distant recurrence-free survival and overall survival. Overall, 369 patients were included: 163 underwent SLNB and 206 underwent ALND. The primary analysis included 78 SLNB and 174 ALND patients with cN1-cN2 disease converted to ycN0. Median follow-up was 55.0 and 55.7 months, respectively. Axillary recurrence occurred in 2.6% after SLNB and 2.3% after ALND (P = 1.000). Local recurrence was 3.8% versus 4.6% (P = 1.000), and locoregional recurrence was 16.7% versus 17.2% (P = 0.911). The 5-year distant recurrence-free survival was 85.7% versus 87.3% (P = 0.851), and 5-year overall survival was 88.7% versus 88.2% (P = 0.506). Patent Blue V-only SLNB after NAC was associated with low axillary recurrence and oncologic outcomes comparable to those with ALND in selected initially node-positive patients downstaged to ycN0, supporting its pragmatic use in public health settings.

papers.abstract: Complete lymph node dissection (CLND) in selected patients with cutaneous malignancies presents anatomical challenges, and current imaging offers limited intraoperative guidance. This pilot study assessed the feasibility of intraoperative augmented reality (AR) visualization of patient-specific, fludeoxyglucose-18 positron emission tomography (FDG-PET/CT) derived three-dimensional (3D) model at predefined stages during CLND. In this prospective pilot study, 16 consecutive patients undergoing CLND for cutaneous malignancies were enrolled. Preoperative FDG-PET/CT datasets were segmented to generate patient-specific 3D model, projected via an AR headset at predefined stages before and during surgery. The median age was 71 years (range 33-79 years); 11 patients had melanoma (68.8%), 4 had Merkel cell carcinoma (25.0%), and 1 had squamous cell carcinoma (6.3%). Eight patients (50%) had received neoadjuvant systemic therapy. Dissection sites included superficial groin (9, 56.3%), deep groin (4, 25.0%), axilla (2, 12.5%), and combined (1, 6.3%). The median largest nodal size on imaging was 32 mm (range 13-65 mm). AR projection was successfully completed in all 16 patients across all predefined surgical stages, with no technical failures or AR-related complications. Mean operative time was 106.2 min (SD ±38.4). Postoperative complications occurred in seven patients (43.8%), consistent with expected rates, including wound infection in six (37.5%) and collection requiring drainage in one (6.3%). Intraoperative AR visualization of patient-specific, FDG-PET/CT-derived 3D models was technically feasible at predefined stages of CLND for cutaneous malignancies. Further studies should assess registration accuracy, workflow, and clinical utility.

papers.abstract: Contrary to intuitive expectations, extensive experimental and clinical evidence indicates that the peripheral immune response induced by cancer vaccines does not reliably correlate with therapeutic efficacy. Here, we explain that this is not simply due to technical limitations, but rather reflects more fundamental biological realities. Current cancer vaccines, particularly those relying on helper epitopes derived from foreign antigens and providing heterologous CD4 T-cell help, amplify circulating CD8 T-cell responses that are ineffective at the tumor site. In contrast, the T-cell responses that mediate tumor regression are frequently undetectable by standard assays, similar to what is often observed in autoimmunity. Consequently, for most tumor antigens, including neoepitopes, immune tolerance can be reliably determined only in vivo, not in vitro. The threshold for a break of tolerance is variable, explaining the contradictory role of "low-avidity" T cells across the literature. We emphasize that the widespread interpretation of a positive immunoassay as evidence of a break in tolerance is mechanistically unsupported. Conversely, the absence of a detectable T-cell response is equally inconclusive, which undermines the use of immunological assays for the preselection of vaccine candidates. Standard immunological assays fail to define reliable biomarkers of therapeutic efficacy, and currently retain value only as mechanistic research tools. They constitute inadequate criteria when adopted as pharmacoimmunodynamic readouts or surrogate endpoints during the optimization, validation, or clinical evaluation of therapeutic cancer vaccines. Candidate vaccines should instead be selected on functional evidence of tolerance reversal in vivo, demonstrated by the induction of on-target tissue damage.

papers.abstract: Ovarian metastases (OM) form a diagnostic challenge since the primary tumour constitutes a heterogeneous group of malignancies. A comprehensive overview of the primary tumour origins of OM and the clinical consequences of OM is currently lacking. This study aims to evaluate the incidence, origin, metastatic patterns, treatment and survival of women with synchronous OM in the Netherlands. Patients with synchronous OM between 2009 and 2023 were identified in the Netherlands Cancer Registry. Treatment was categorised as curative-intent treatment, palliative systemic therapy, or best supportive care. Cox regression analyses were performed to assess factors associated with overall survival. A total of 1559 patients with synchronous OM were identified. Colorectal cancer was the most common primary tumour (47.2%), followed by gastric (14.1%) and appendiceal cancer (10.2%). Most patients (85.1%) presented with OM in com bination with other metastatic sites, most frequently peritoneal metastases (28.9%), while 14.9% had solitary OM. Survival varied by primary tumour location, ranging from a median overall survival of 45.1 months in appendiceal cancer, 17.5 months in colorectal cancer, to 4.0 months in gastric cancer. Median overall survival of the entire cohort was 25.3 months for solitary OM (range 19.6-34.1 months) and 12.9 months for patients with additional metastatic sites (range 12.0-13.7 months). This study demonstrates that in the Netherlands, OM most commonly originate from colorectal cancer. Primary tumour location is the main determinant of prognosis and outcomes in selected patients may be more favourable than previously assumed.

papers.abstract: Among hospitalized cancer patients, persistent fever despite intravenous antibiotics often triggers treatment escalation and additional diagnostics. Earlier identification of patients at low risk for ongoing fever could support more selective decision-making. We developed and compared multimodal AI frameworks to predict persistent fever at the 48-72-hour reassessment window. Models integrated structured variables, time-series, notes, and chest imaging. Models were developed in a University Hospital Essen cohort and evaluated using holdout validation, two pooled regional hospitals, and MIMIC-IV ICU. A feature-level tabularized multimodal TabPFN model showed consistent discrimination, with AUC 0.84 (95% CI, 0.81-0.86) in cross-validation, 0.82 (95% CI, 0.77-0.87) in holdout validation, and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.74-0.81) in MIMIC-IV; other multimodal strategies showed comparable but more variable performance. Performance was primarily driven by temperature dynamics, while chest-radiograph imaging provided no incremental predictive value. In a clinician validation study, the multimodal model outperformed clinicians (Trial 1 balanced accuracy: 0.77 vs 0.60; Trial 2: 0.79 vs 0.57), while clinician balanced accuracy reached 0.71 (95% CI 0.67-0.75) in the AI-assisted condition, suggesting potential benefit of AI support. Overall, multimodal AI demonstrates potential to support 48-hour antibiotic reassessment and stewardship-oriented decision-making, although further prospective studies are needed.

papers.abstract: To prospectively evaluate stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for oligoprogressive lesions from oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma (omRCC) during first-line systemic therapy. This single-arm, phase II trial (ChiCTR2000032947) enrolled RCC patients with up to 3 progressive lesions and maximum 5 total metastases during first-line systemic therapy. Current first-line systemic therapy was maintained while all oligoprogressive lesions were treated with SBRT. The primary endpoint was the 6-month progression-free survival (PFS), tested against a historical null benchmark of ≤50% versus an alternative of ≥70% using a one-sided exact binomial test. Secondary endpoints included local control (LC) rate, time to second-line therapy (TTST), overall survival (OS), safety and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Thirty-nine patients with 53 progressive lesions were enrolled. The 1-year and 2-year LC rate was 97.9% (95% CI: 94.0-100) and 84.6% (95% CI: 72.8-98.3). With median follow-up of 24.0 months (interquartile range 14.0-42.3 months), the 6-month PFS was 89.7% (95% CI: 80.7-99.8), successfully meeting the primary endpoint by significantly exceeding the 50% historical benchmark (p<0.001). The 12-month PFS was 59.0% (95% CI: 45.4-76.6). The 6-month and 12-month TTST were 5.1% (95% CI: 0-12.1) and 35.9% (95% CI: 20.6-51.2), respectively. The 2-year OS was 76.8% (95% CI: 63.8-92.6). No grade ≥3 SBRT-related adverse events and no decline of HRQoL were observed. SBRT for oligoprogressive omRCC is a safe strategy that yields favorable PFS and delays TTST without compromising HRQoL. A larger-scale randomized controlled trial is warranted.

papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are abundant in the tumor microenvironment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and exert pivotal pro-tumorigenic functions, including extracellular matrix remodeling, angiogenesis, and immunosuppression. In this study, we investigated the molecular mechanisms by which CAFs orchestrate the recruitment and functional polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) to drive HNSCC progression. Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), a key regulator of CAFs, exhibited a markedly positive correlation with CD163+ macrophage infiltration in human HNSCC tissues. Functional validation demonstrated that NNMT mediated CAF-driven recruitment and M2 polarization of TAMs in HNSCC in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, NNMT upregulated CCL2 secretion in CAFs, facilitating CCR2-dependent TAM recruitment and M2 polarization in HNSCC. Moreover, NNMT activated the PI3K/Akt pathway, leading to upregulation of the EBF transcription factor 1 (EBF1), which directly regulates CCL2 transcription in CAFs. Furthermore, the combination of NNMT inhibitors and anti-PD-1 antibodies synergistically suppressed tumor growth and modulated anti-tumor immunity in a syngeneic mouse model. In conclusion, these findings reveal that the NNMT/PI3K/Akt/EBF1 signaling axis contributes to CAF-mediated TAM recruitment and M2 polarization in HNSCC through the CCL2/CCR2 axis. Our study sheds new light on CAF-macrophage crosstalk in HNSCC and provides potential therapeutic strategies for patients.

papers.abstract: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024-2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024-2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination.

papers.abstract: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) causes B-cell lymphomas and endothelial malignancies, yet no prophylactic treatments exist. Developing antivirals requires better understanding of KSHV infection mechanisms, including the identity of KSHV receptors on B cells and the synergistic role of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) co-infection. We investigated the role of heparan sulphate proteoglycans (HSPGs) in KSHV B cell infection using a KSHV mutant lacking the HSPG-binding glycoprotein K8.1 (KSHVΔK8.1), surface-HSPG profiling, and HSPG mimetics. We assessed whether EBV enhances KSHV infection via HSPG upregulation or entry facilitation, and tested HSPG mimetics prophylactically against KSHV and EBV infection in male and female humanised NSG mice. Lacking K8.1 delayed KSHV B cell infection (K2 expression, 24 h: p = 0.0074). Surface HSPG decreased following KSHV infection (6 versus 72 h: p = 0.0003) while pre-treating KSHV with HSPG mimetics inhibited infection (K2 expression, 24 h: p = 0.0097 and 0.0001). EBV co-infection enhanced neither HSPG expression (6 versus 72 h: p = 0.61) nor KSHV entry (p = 0.59). HSPG mimetics differed mechanistically: sulphated cyclodextrins (sulphated-β-CDs) inhibited infection while preserving virions, whereas sulfonated cyclodextrins (M11S-β-CDs) were virucidal. Both reduced KSHV infection in vitro, only M11S-β-CDs efficiently inhibited EBV. In humanised mice, prophylactic M11S-β-CDs reduced KSHV (p = 0.0072), but not EBV (p = 0.88) infection. HSPGs facilitate early KSHV B cell infection, but EBV-mediated enhancement is independent of HSPG upregulation or entry facilitation. HSPG mimetics inhibited KSHV more effectively than EBV, supporting virucidal M11S-β-cyclodextrins as promising prophylactics against lytic KSHV infection. papers.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) are approved for first-line maintenance in advanced ovarian cancer, but no homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) assay is approved in China, and additional biomarkers are needed. The MEDx-HRDetectCDx assay integrates genome-wide genomic instability profiling, whole-genome doubling (WGD) status, and homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene mutation detection. Analytical performance was validated with national reference materials and a head-to-head comparison with Myriad myChoice™ HRD-Plus. Clinical performance was evaluated in women receiving first-line niraparib maintenance in the prospective, multicentre RENI-1 study (NCT04986371). The primary endpoint of this exploratory biomarker analysis was progression-free survival (PFS) by HRD versus homologous recombination proficient (HRp) status. Other candidate biomarkers were exploratory. HRD classification achieved an overall concordance of 97.1% (95% CI: 85.08%-99.48%) with Myriad myChoice™ HRD-Plus. Among 102 patients with assessable HRD status, median PFS was numerically longer with HRD than HRp tumours (not reached versus 14.4 months). However, the primary endpoint was not met (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; 95% CI: 0.35-1.03; P = 0.066). In exploratory subgroup analyses not adjusted for multiplicity, HRR mutations (HR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.25-0.86; nominal P = 0.014) and WGD-negative status (HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.29-0.94; nominal P = 0.029) were associated with longer median PFS. The MEDx-HRDetectCDx assay showed robust analytical performance. Although the prespecified clinical validation criteria were not met, integrating WGD with HRD or HRR status identified subgroups with favourable first-line maintenance outcomes in exploratory analyses, warranting randomised validation. papers.abstract: Population-derived target ranges of drug concentrations or EEG indices are commonly used in clinical practice for the titration of anaesthesia. By definition, this inevitably results in a relative overdose for most patients and an underdose for a few. For accurate individualised titration of anaesthesia, suitable within-subject targets need to be established. To be reliable, these targets require a measurable EEG response to changes in the hypnotic drug concentration, an EEG endpoint that reliably indicates absence of consciousness, and stability in the EEG drug-dose response relationship so that it is not influenced by other factors that might change through the course of the operation.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and lethal malignancies, representing a major global health concern. Viral hepatitis, metabolic associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD)-related hepatitis, and alcoholic hepatitis are three critical precursor lesions that can progress to HCC. Owing to its insidious onset, HCC is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage, where surgical intervention is no longer feasible. This underscores the pivotal role of systemic therapies, including targeted therapy, in improving patient outcomes. Over the past decade, the first-line systemic treatment landscape for advanced HCC has progressed from a single approved tyrosine-kinase inhibitor (sorafenib) to a range of targeted agents and, more recently, targeted-immunotherapy combinations. In randomized phase III trials, first-line combination regimens such as atezolizumab plus bevacizumab have improved median overall survival to 19.2 months versus 13.4 months with sorafenib (HR = 0.66, 95%CI: 0.52-0.85), extending survival beyond the range historically achieved with single-agent targeted therapy. The evolution from initial single-agent targeted therapy to current targeted-immunotherapy combinations reflects the ever-evolving therapeutic strategies and deepened understanding of HCC pathogenesis. Further investigation into the signaling pathways and molecular targets of HCC is crucial for advancing precision medicine in this malignancy. Herein, we comprehensively review the tumor microenvironment (TME), key signaling pathways, and approved targeted-immunotherapy regimens for HCC, including agents approved by the US FDA and, where FDA approval is absent, by other regulators such as China's NMPA (sintilimab plus IBI305, camrelizumab plus apatinib, and the LEAP-012 regimen). We also discuss early-phase clinical trials of promising agents, drug resistance and safety concerns in targeted-immunotherapy, as well as future research directions.
